candidates.buyer: Incorporated associations: churches, sports and community clubs, NGOs, trade groups, overseas nonprofits operating in PNG

NBC report that only 1 of 162 Milne Bay associations had re-registered: https://www.nbc.com.pg/post/38508/ipa-launches-awareness-campaign-in-milne-bay-over-new-associations-law . Act text: https://pacliirms.austlii.edu.au/pg/legis/num_act/aia2023307
candidates.existing: IPA online registry is free and re-registration costs nothing. IPA runs awareness teams on the ground. The competitor search found no dedicated compliance service for churches or clubs. Accountants and law firms (KPMG, Ashurst) have published notes only.
candidates.known_note: K09 rejected household employers, PMV and market vendors only; associations are a different buyer group and a new duty.
candidates.name: Association re-registration and annual compliance pack under the Associations Incorporation Act 2023
candidates.trigger: Associations Incorporation Act 2023, in force 1 July 2026. Re-register on the IPA online registry by 30 June 2027 or be removed from the register. After that: annual return each year, committee of at least 3 with 1 resident, accounting records, audited statements above thresholds, beneficial-ownership register, new financial penalties.
candidates.unchecked: How many associations are registered. Whether the online portal works for rural committees. Willingness to pay (the mass of buyers are churches and clubs with little cash). Audit thresholds and beneficial-ownership detail from the Act text. Whether a done-for-you or agent model is allowed. The cut-off date is a one-off rush, so recurring revenue depends on annual returns.

coverage.category: 1. Household employers: domestic workers, live-in carers, nannies
coverage.found: No PNG statute specific to household employment found. Compulsory super applies only to employers of 15 or more (inference: households fall outside). PNGTUC has asked for domestic worker protections and a minimum wage. Nothing new beyond K09.

coverage.category: 2. Scrap-metal dealers
coverage.found: One search returned only other countries' laws (Fiji, Zambia, UK, NZ). No PNG scrap-metal licensing regime found, so unverified whether one exists.

coverage.category: 3. Second-hand dealers and pawnbrokers
coverage.found: Second-hand Dealers Act (Ch. 322) and Pawnbrokers Act (Ch. 93) exist on PacLII. Licensing is by Police, or Public Health for clothing. Licensees must keep a purchase record book and hold goods for 3 days. NCDC trading licence page lists K250 for second-hand dealers. Small, old, paper-based regime.

coverage.category: 4. Gold and jewellery buyers
coverage.found: Domestic gold trade has been open since the 1987 deregulation. Only export is licensed, by BPNG (K25,000 paid-up capital, K75,000 bond, annual licence). That is covered by K04. No separate domestic buyer duty found.

coverage.category: 5. Used car parts and vehicle dismantlers
coverage.found: No dedicated search. Budget used. One RTA hit says its new IT system will cover licensing of motor car dealers and inspection stations; dismantlers were not checked.

coverage.category: 6. Livestock traders, markets and animal transport
coverage.found: Only a colonial-era livestock movement regulation (1951) and NAQIA import permits found. No current domestic movement permit regime confirmed. Nothing actionable.

coverage.category: 7. Small abattoirs and butchers
coverage.found: Slaughtering Act 1964 and Slaughtering Regulation 1965: slaughterhouse licence (K20 a year) and a mandatory daily slaughter record book, with meat inspectors. Current administrator (NAQIA or other) not confirmed. Very small, paper-based market.

coverage.category: 8. Beekeepers
coverage.found: No search spent. Budget. PNG apiculture is minor and no registration duty was seen.

coverage.category: 9. Veterinary practices and veterinary medicine sellers
coverage.found: Veterinary Surgeons Act 1966 sets a Board and Register run by a department Registrar. No veterinary medicines registration or dealer scheme found. Tiny buyer group.

coverage.category: 10. Well drillers and water abstraction
coverage.found: Water use is vested in the State (Environment Act 2000 s79). CEPA issues environment permits for water extraction. The Water Resources Regulation 1982 has unconfirmed status. No borehole driller licence found.

coverage.category: 11. Septic, sanitation and waste haulers
coverage.found: Local governments contract private collectors in towns. CEPA has a permit to discharge waste. No septic-hauler register or recurring report found.

coverage.category: 12. Lift, boiler and pressure-equipment owners and inspectors
coverage.found: Only the Industrial Safety (Lifts) Order 1968 under the Industrial Safety, Health and Welfare Act 1961 was found. Current inspection and certificate practice, and boiler rules, are unverified.

coverage.category: 13. Small water systems
coverage.found: No search spent. Budget.

coverage.category: 14. Pesticide and fertiliser dealers and applicators
coverage.found: Environmental Contaminants (Pesticides) Regulation 1988 under the Environmental Contaminants Act 1978 requires a permit to import, distribute or sell pesticides (K20 application, K100 grant) and records of imports and sales. Administering agency and current enforcement unconfirmed. No fertiliser regime found.

coverage.category: 15. Labour contractors and recruitment agencies
coverage.found: Employment Act (Ch. 373) defines employment agents and worker-recruiters. A PNG firm claims an Employment Agents Licence from the Department of Labour. The Department is the only authorised recruiter for the Australian seasonal worker programme. No recurring-report duty found.

coverage.category: 16. Cemeteries, burial societies and funeral services
coverage.found: Cemeteries Act (Ch. 302): the Minister licenses private burial grounds, e.g. for churches. The Act is under law-reform review. NCDC has acted against a funeral home. No funeral director licence or recurring filing found.

coverage.category: 17. Community and religious bodies: associations, charities, halal and kosher supervision
coverage.found: Strong finding. Associations Incorporation Act 2023 commences 1 July 2026. Every incorporated association, and overseas nonprofits, must re-register online by 30 June 2027, or be removed from the register (restorable for 2 years with a late fee). New duties: public/members-benefit subtype, at least 3 committee members with 1 resident, audited accounts above thresholds, annual returns, beneficial-ownership register. IPA says only 1 of 162 Milne Bay associations had re-registered. Halal and kosher not applicable.

coverage.category: 18. Transport operators: minibus, taxi, moto-taxi, small trucking and bus fleets
coverage.found: The RTA licenses PMVs, taxis and private hire cars (Form 13, renewal needs registration, roadworthiness and fit-and-proper proof). Single-province operations are licensed by the provincial government. A new cloud RTA system is to cover PMV, taxi, freight and dealer licensing. Enforcement drive announced for April 2026. Cash-based sector; see K09.

coverage.category: 19. Market traders, street vendors, money changers
coverage.found: BPNG lists about 9 licensed money changers (Oct 2025), too few to sell to. NCDC trading licences are annual and issued in person, with market stalls charged K5 a day. Informal, per K09.

coverage.category: 20. Small licensed premises with inspections: tattoo studios, driving schools, childminders and nurseries, small food producers, hunting outfitters
coverage.found: No driving-school or instructor licence found on the RTA site. No childcare licensing framework found; early childhood services are still being set up with UNICEF. Small food producers not searched. Tattoo studios and hunting outfitters not applicable.

coverage.category: 21. Fuel stations and fuel or LPG distributors
coverage.found: One search. ICCC regulates maximum retail prices of petrol, diesel, kerosene and Jet A1 under the Prices Regulation Act (Ch. 320), with station price inspections; the pricing arrangements found ran to Dec 2019 and I could not confirm renewal. No fuel retailer licence or recurring filing register found for retailers or LPG distributors. Nothing new.

coverage.category: 22. Grain, coffee, cocoa and other commodity traders, millers and warehouses
coverage.found: Coffee and cocoa dealers are covered by K08 (rejected) and K02. No search spent on other commodities (copra, vanilla, oil palm smallholders) beyond a note that they exist; nothing new beyond K02/K08.

coverage.category: 23. Co-operatives, credit unions and savings groups
coverage.found: BPNG licenses Savings and Loan Societies under the Savings and Loan Societies Act 2015 (licensed list dated 31 Oct 2025, e.g. Alekano SLS, Air Niugini SLS). BPNG says new SLS prudential standards are coming, and an IFC project supports them. Candidate C1. Co-operative societies registry not checked.

coverage.category: 24. Private clinics, labs and other health providers that bill insurers or state schemes
coverage.found: PNG Medical Board licenses private health facilities (EMTV, undated). A Medical Registration Bill amendment was mooted. No insurer or state-scheme billing duty found. Nothing actionable.

coverage.category: 25. Pharmacies, medicine importers, and users of controlled chemicals or precursors
coverage.found: Medicines and Cosmetics Act 1999 covers pharmacy registration, licence term, suspension and inspectors, and the Pharmacy Board registers suppliers. No renewal cycle, fees or enforcement news found (two searches). Candidate C9 is unverified.

coverage.category: 26. Security, cleaning and manpower agencies, and the firms that hire their workers
coverage.found: Security Industries Authority (Security (Protection) Industry Act 2004) licenses firms and guards: 562 licensed firms and 29,445 guards by Dec 2022. Compliance is partial, and unlicensed firms are referred to IRC for GST on fees. DLIR runs compliance workshops. No separate labour-hire licence found. Candidate C2.

coverage.category: 27. Construction, mining and quarry contractors and suppliers: site registers, accreditation, local-content reports
coverage.found: National Procurement Act 2018 and NPC: contracts over PGK500k go through NPC, citizens get exclusive bidding under PGK10m, 50% local content for PGK10-30m, and margins of preference. No contractor accreditation register or periodic local-content filing found. I could not confirm whether the Act is in force from the results. Nothing new.

coverage.category: 28. Notaries, land agents, real estate brokers and other professionals with periodic or anti-money-laundering reports
coverage.found: AML/CTF Act 2015: DNFBPs include real estate agents, precious metals and stones dealers, lawyers and notaries on client transactions, TCSPs and motor vehicle dealers. They register with FASU under s.57 (public register: 202 DNFBPs as at March 2026) and file suspicious matter reports under s.41. FASU supervision of DNFBPs is described as weak, and PNG was grey-listed by FATF (Feb 2026 per a secondary source; the conference communique acknowledges it). Candidate C3.

coverage.category: 29. Hotels, guest houses and short-term rentals: guest registers, tourism levies
coverage.found: The TPA Act 1993 is under review. A draft PNG Tourism Bill 2026 (v1.0, 3 July 2026) has an accreditation regime with application, renewal and rating. Current accommodation licence rules were not confirmed. Candidate C7 is weak and depends on enactment.

coverage.category: 30. Small exporters and importers facing traceability or certification rules: food, fish, timber, forest-risk commodities
coverage.found: NFA export applications are weighed against the company's export returns record; EU fish exports need catch certificates and onshore processing, but the sector is tuna-dominated and large. EUDR small-operator date was reported as moving to 30 Dec 2026 (needs checking). PNGFA permit rules were not found. Candidate C8. Coffee and cocoa are under K02.

coverage.category: 31. Corporate registry (IPA): annual returns, re-registration, beneficial ownership
coverage.found: Companies Act 2022 amendment required all entities to re-register within 12 months (from Dec 2022) and late annual returns can lead to deregistration. A Companies (Amendment) Act 2025 on beneficial ownership registers, bearer shares and nominees was consulted in Sept 2025 (a FATF response). Gazettal not confirmed. Candidate C4.

coverage.category: 32. ICT regulation: SIM card registration and agents (NICTA)
coverage.found: NICTA consulted on a Draft SIM Card Registration (Amendment and Consolidation) Regulation 2026, to align with the National Digital Identity Policy and SevisPass; consultation closed Feb/Mar 2026. Retailer and agent duties are unknown. Candidate C5 is weak.

coverage.category: 33. Gaming and betting (National Gaming Control Board)
coverage.found: Gaming Control Act 2007 and Gaming Machines Regulation 2015 (confirm still in force). Gaming machine operator licences run 3 years (commercial guide) and there are technician licences. A new Gaming Control Bill is awaiting ministerial review, and a first casino is planned. Candidate C6 is weak.

coverage.category: 34. Employment of non-citizens (DLIR work permits)
coverage.found: Employment of Non-Citizens Act 2007 and Regulation 2008: employers keep a Register of Work Permits, run labour market tests and training and localisation plans, and renew permits; a work permit portal exists (workpermits.gov.pg). Candidate C10 is weak.

coverage.category: 35. Workers' compensation (Office of Workers Compensation)
coverage.found: Workers' Compensation Act (Ch. 179) makes the employer liable and sets up an Office of Workers' Compensation, an Insurance Commissioner and a Fund. Employer registration, insurance and filing duties could not be confirmed (one search, no official source). Candidate C11 is unverified.

coverage.category: 36. Liquor licensing (provincial liquor licensing commissions)
coverage.found: One search returned no PNG results at all (only Vanuatu, Australia, Canada, South Africa). Not verified; needs a narrower search and the Liquor Licensing Act text.

coverage.category: 37. Alluvial gold dealers and artisanal miners (MRA / Mining Act)
coverage.found: BPNG issues annual (1-year) gold export licences and publishes a 2024 list. The Mining Act has alluvial miner permits and a gold dealer licence. A citizens-only alluvial policy was reported but not confirmed. Related to K04 but a different buyer group (dealers and buyers). Candidate C12.
